title: Trout-Cabrera Was Simple Compared With PCA-Ohtani
contentHtml:
Most MVP races come with their share of debate, if not simply to give talking heads something to fill the endless airtime with. But one of most legitimately polarizing MVP arguments in baseball history played out right in front of us in 2012, when Miguel Cabrera and Mike Trout went toe-to-toe for the American League’s top honor. Cabrera-Trout had it all — hitting versus defense, tradition versus sabermetrics, Triple Crowns versus massive WAR tallies — and in retrospect, changed the MVP conversation forever.

Subscribe now

Flash-forward by 14 years, and there’s another MVP debate playing out that could be just as historically significant: Shohei Ohtani versus Pete Crow-Armstrong. The two have been battling back and forth for about a month now — with epic head-to-head duels in addition to tit-for-tats from afar — as PCA has made things a dead heat in the odds at the beginning of August — and even pulled slightly ahead of Ohtani over the past week:

But this race is far from over. Not only do Ohtani’s Dodgers and PCA’s Cubs have around 30 games apiece remaining on their schedules, but the especially complicated nature of this comparison — even relative to something like Trout versus Cabrera in the previous generation — ought to make the debate itself over value be a central factor in how this MVP race is remembered.
